To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of fluoroquinolone antibiotics in the treatment of lower respiratory tract infection in the elderly is effective and safe.
the treatment of exacerbations of chronic bronchitis with fluoroquinolone is effective and safe.
the use of ciprofloxin in the treatment of lower respiratory tract infection in the elderly was effective and safe.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) treatment in elderly patients (EP).
the problem of the treatment of lower respiratory tract infectious in elderly patients.
the treatment of exacerbations of chronic bronchitis in the elderly patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ciprofloxacine is an effective and safe drug for the treatment of lower respiratory tract infection in the elderly.
the use of fluoroquinolone antibiotics for treatment of lower respiratory tract infection in the elderly is a reasonable and effective alternative to the use of the traditional antimicrobial drugs.
fluoroquinolone antibiotics are the first line treatment for elderly patients with acute exacerbation of chronic bronchitis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fluoroquinolone antibiotics are effective and well tolerated in patients with lower respiratory tract infection.
the use of ofloxacin in a single dose regimen is more effective and less expensive.
of the three antibiotics tested, ciprofloxin was the most effective in the treatment of lower respiratory tract infection in the elderly.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have demonstrated the ability to use a single cell-based assay to measure the effect of a drug on multiple pathways simultaneously, which can provide a more complete understanding of the mechanism of action.
the use of fluoroquinolone antibiotics should be limited in the elderly patients with exacerbated chronic bronchiitis.

the use of antibiotics in the treatment of lower respiratory tract infection in the elderly patients should be individualized and based upon the patient's clinical status and the microbiological results of the respiratory tract specimens.
